### What does this PR do?

Adds a DeepSeek-V4-**Pro** GRPO example and a "Running DeepSeek-V4-Pro at scale" section to the DeepSeek V4 guide. The Flash example and docs cover the 40-layer model on 8 nodes; Pro (61 layers, 384 routed experts, ~1.6 T parameters) runs through the same integration but needs a different scale and a few memory levers, and the first run otherwise costs a lot of node-hours of trial and error (it did for us).

- `examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_pro_megatron.sh`: derived from `run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron.sh` with identical algorithm / data / reward settings and two hardware profiles selected by an env toggle (`HW=h100`: 64 × 8 H100 80 GB, PP32 × EP8, rollout TP8 × DP8 × EP64; `HW=gb200`: 64 × 4 GB200, PP16 × EP16, rollout DP32 × EP32). Every knob that differs from Flash carries the reason in a comment.
- `docs/advance/deepseek_v4_integration.rst`: topology (cross-node rollout replicas, PP layout with the hash layers in stage 0), the host-memory model under all-CPU optimizer offload and the three levers (bf16 grad buffers, precision-aware optimizer, `optimizer_offload_fraction`), checkpoint options and their sizes, rollout kernel choices for a native DSV4 checkpoint, what the DAPO reward measures on Pro, and the measured numbers for both profiles.

- `verl/models/mcore/patch.py` + `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: the precision-aware optimizer on a quantized checkpoint needs two Megatron-LM fixes that are still open — no-grad fp32 main-param shards (NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#8245; otherwise `optimizer_cpu_offload=True` raises `can't optimize a non-leaf Tensor`) and per-dtype grad-norm / clipping kernels (NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7279; otherwise the mixed bf16/fp32 gradient list hits an illegal memory access). Their runtime equivalents are applied once per process before the optimizer is built, in the same place as the existing MCore patches (`VERL_MEGATRON_OPTIMIZER_COMPAT=0` disables them); a single-dtype gradient list is forwarded to the original Megatron functions unchanged, so the default optimizer path is untouched. Covered by CPU tests.

Dependencies called out in the script header and the doc: #8234 (cross-node vLLM data-parallel replicas) and #8235 (resuming an offloaded optimizer) — **both merged on 2026-10-26** (3dd97a0e, 0bd668c1), so verl `main` at or after those commits is all the example needs.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+deepseek+v4+pro — none; #6864 and the Flash example cover Flash only.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

- `python3 tests/special_sanity/check_example_naming.py` and `check_docs_time_info.py` pass; `bash -n` on the script; both profiles expand to the intended topology; `tests/utils/megatron/test_optimizer_compat_patches_on_cpu.py` (3 new CPU tests) and the existing `test_vllm_mxfp4_restage_on_cpu.py` pass in the megatron/vllm venv.
- GB200, verl `main@a4b9354` + #8234, Megatron-Bridge 0.6.2, vLLM 0.29.0 (image built from `verlai/verl:uv.cu130.dev3` for aarch64):
  - 4-layer truncated Pro, 8 nodes, GRPO 2 steps: verl's default backend (`--moe_backend deep_gemm --linear_backend deep_gemm` via #8308) 2/2 steps, rollout/actor log-prob Pearson 0.9992 / 0.9992, refit 8 s; `ROLLOUT_MOE_BACKEND=marlin` 2/2 steps, Pearson 0.9994 / 0.9994, refit 8.6 s.
  - 61-layer Pro, `HW=gb200` profile (64 nodes, PP16 × EP16, rollout DP32 × EP32, response 8192, R3, Marlin), 3 steps: steady step 960 / 972 s (first 1991 s), `gen` ≈500 s, `update_weights` ≈251 s, Pearson 0.9981 / 0.9983 / 0.9980, actor GPU 63.8 GB, head-node host peak 929 GB. With verl's default `moe_backend=deep_gemm` the same configuration dies in vLLM's profiling run (`CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in DeepGEMM `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous` at 10,240 batched tokens; it runs at 4,096 batched tokens but ≈24 % slower in `gen` than Marlin) — see #8381.
- H100 (64 × 8 H100 80 GB), verl `main@a4b9354` + #8234, `HW=h100` profile (PP32 × EP8, rollout TP8 × DP8 × EP64, response 4096, R3, Marlin), 3 steps: steady step 692 / 684 s (first step 2585 s with JIT), `gen` ≈280 s, `update_weights` ≈235 s, Pearson 0.9982 / 0.9985 / 0.9983, actor GPU 25.5–26.2 GB, host peak 558 GB on the two stage-0 nodes (244–409 GB elsewhere). With verl's default `moe_backend=deep_gemm` the same run fails at vLLM `load_model` (`Mxfp4 MoE backend 'DEEPGEMM_MXFP4' does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support current device cuda`, SM90) — hence the Marlin default in the script.
- Earlier validation of the same configuration on pinned verl `1d367a4f` (GB200) and `45a40312` (H100), including a 40-step segmented run, save/resume at 64 and 128 nodes and the reward analysis quoted in the doc, is summarised in the doc section.

### API and Usage Example

No API change.

```bash
# 64 nodes x 8 H100
HW=h100 MODEL_PATH=... TRAIN_FILE=... TEST_FILE=... bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_pro_megatron.sh
# 64 nodes x 4 GB200, actor from a Megatron dist-checkpoint, precision-aware optimizer so that 64 nodes can save
HW=gb200 DIST_CKPT_PATH=... PRECISION_AWARE_OPTIMIZER=True SAVE_FREQ=20 bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_pro_megatron.sh
```

### Design & Code Changes

- One script, two profiles: the naming check forbids hardware variants in the file name, so the profile is an env toggle that only sets defaults; every value can still be overridden.
- The two Megatron-Core compatibility patches follow the pattern of the existing patches in `verl/models/mcore/patch.py` (applied from the Megatron engine's `__init__`, idempotent, env-disableable) and drop out as no-ops once the upstream fixes land; `make_dtype_safe_grad_fns` / `wrap_no_grad` are plain helpers so the logic is unit-testable without a GPU.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting).
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s): not feasible in CI (64-node, 1.6 T model); validated by the runs listed under Test.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.

@linmuchuiyang It's unexpected that vLLM can't enable DeepGEMM for DeepSeek-V4 both in Hopper/Blackwell, let me have a check.

@aoshen02 @ISEEKYAN done train-rollout kernel bitwise alignment on DeepSeek-V4 in https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-14-train-inference-consistency, I think they used deep_gemm kernel for both linear and moe.

@wuxibin89 Thanks for looking. I believe the difference is the checkpoint, not the kernel:

- The recipe in that blog trains **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base**, whose routed experts are FP8 (`"expert_dtype": "fp8"` in its `config.json`; the post says "the routed experts' FP8 grouped GEMM"). For that checkpoint vLLM runs DeepGEMM's FP8 grouped GEMM for the MoE, which exists on SM90 and SM100, so `linear_backend=deep_gemm` + `moe_backend=deep_gemm` is the right default on both — and the change proposed in #8381 keeps it for every `expert_dtype: fp8` model.
- The post-trained **DeepSeek-V4-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Pro** ship MXFP4 experts (`"expert_dtype": "fp4"`). For them vLLM maps `moe_backend=deep_gemm` to `DeepGemmFP4Experts` (`m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous`), whose `_supports_current_device` requires SM100 or SM120 (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/deep_gemm_moe.py`, unchanged in v0.32.0). That is the H100 `load_model` error in #8381; the FP8 dense layers still use DeepGEMM there (`--linear_backend deep_gemm` stays).
- On GB200 the FP4 DeepGEMM path does run for Pro: fine at 4,096 batched tokens (8297634), `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in `profile_run` at 10,240 (8183203), and ~24 % slower generation than Marlin where it runs. That part may well be a vLLM/DeepGEMM bug as you suspect; we will re-run it on vLLM 0.32.0 (#8390) and report in #8381.

So the example keeps `moe_backend=marlin` for the MXFP4 experts of the released Pro checkpoint, and `linear_backend` at verl's DeepGEMM default.

### What does this PR do?

Adds a DeepSeek-V4-**Pro** GRPO example and a "Running DeepSeek-V4-Pro at scale" section to the DeepSeek V4 guide. The Flash example and docs cover the 40-layer model on 8 nodes; Pro (61 layers, 384 routed experts, ~1.6 T parameters) runs through the same integration but needs a different scale and a few memory levers, and the first run otherwise costs a lot of node-hours of trial and error (it did for us).

- `examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_pro_megatron.sh`: derived from `run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron.sh` with identical algorithm / data / reward settings and two hardware profiles selected by an env toggle (`HW=h100`: 64 × 8 H100 80 GB, PP32 × EP8, rollout TP8 × DP8 × EP64; `HW=gb200`: 64 × 4 GB200, PP16 × EP16, rollout DP32 × EP32). Every knob that differs from Flash carries the reason in a comment.
- `docs/advance/deepseek_v4_integration.rst`: topology (cross-node rollout replicas, PP layout with the hash layers in stage 0), the host-memory model under all-CPU optimizer offload and the three levers (bf16 grad buffers, precision-aware optimizer, `optimizer_offload_fraction`), checkpoint options and their sizes, rollout kernel choices for a native DSV4 checkpoint, what the DAPO reward measures on Pro, and the measured numbers for both profiles.

- `verl/models/mcore/patch.py` + `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: the precision-aware optimizer on a quantized checkpoint needs two Megatron-LM fixes that are still open — no-grad fp32 main-param shards (NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#8245; otherwise `optimizer_cpu_offload=True` raises `can't optimize a non-leaf Tensor`) and per-dtype grad-norm / clipping kernels (NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7279; otherwise the mixed bf16/fp32 gradient list hits an illegal memory access). Their runtime equivalents are applied once per process before the optimizer is built, in the same place as the existing MCore patches (`VERL_MEGATRON_OPTIMIZER_COMPAT=0` disables them); a single-dtype gradient list is forwarded to the original Megatron functions unchanged, so the default optimizer path is untouched. Covered by CPU tests.

Dependencies called out in the script header and the doc: #8234 (cross-node vLLM data-parallel replicas) and #8235 (resuming an offloaded optimizer) — **both merged on 2026-10-26** (3dd97a0e, 0bd668c1), so verl `main` at or after those commits is all the example needs.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+deepseek+v4+pro — none; #6864 and the Flash example cover Flash only.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

- `python3 tests/special_sanity/check_example_naming.py` and `check_docs_time_info.py` pass; `bash -n` on the script; both profiles expand to the intended topology; `tests/utils/megatron/test_optimizer_compat_patches_on_cpu.py` (3 new CPU tests) and the existing `test_vllm_mxfp4_restage_on_cpu.py` pass in the megatron/vllm venv.
- GB200, verl `main@a4b9354` + #8234, Megatron-Bridge 0.6.2, vLLM 0.29.0 (image built from `verlai/verl:uv.cu130.dev3` for aarch64):
  - 4-layer truncated Pro, 8 nodes, GRPO 2 steps: verl's default backend (`--moe_backend deep_gemm --linear_backend deep_gemm` via #8308) 2/2 steps, rollout/actor log-prob Pearson 0.9992 / 0.9992, refit 8 s; `ROLLOUT_MOE_BACKEND=marlin` 2/2 steps, Pearson 0.9994 / 0.9994, refit 8.6 s.

With verl's default `moe_backend=deep_gemm` the same configuration dies in vLLM's profiling run (`CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in DeepGEMM `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous` at 10,240 batched tokens; it runs at 4,096 batched tokens but ≈24 % slower in `gen` than Marlin) — see #8381.
- H100 (64 × 8 H100 80 GB), verl `main@a4b9354` + #8234, `HW=h100` profile (PP32 × EP8, rollout TP8 × DP8 × EP64, response 4096, R3, Marlin), 3 steps: steady step 692 / 684 s (first step 2585 s with JIT), `gen` ≈280 s, `update_weights` ≈235 s, Pearson 0.9982 / 0.9985 / 0.9983, actor GPU 25.5–26.2 GB, host peak 558 GB on the two stage-0 nodes (244–409 GB elsewhere). ### API and Usage Example

No API change.

```bash
# 64 nodes x 8 H100
HW=h100 MODEL_PATH=... TRAIN_FILE=... TEST_FILE=... bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_pro_megatron.sh
# 64 nodes x 4 GB200, actor from a Megatron dist-checkpoint, precision-aware optimizer so that 64 nodes can save
HW=gb200 DIST_CKPT_PATH=... PRECISION_AWARE_OPTIMIZER=True SAVE_FREQ=20 bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_pro_megatron.sh
```

### Design & Code Changes

- One script, two profiles: the naming check forbids hardware variants in the file name, so the profile is an env toggle that only sets defaults; every value can still be overridden.
- The two Megatron-Core compatibility patches follow the pattern of the existing patches in `verl/models/mcore/patch.py` (applied from the Megatron engine's `__init__`, idempotent, env-disableable) and drop out as no-ops once the upstream fixes land; `make_dtype_safe_grad_fns` / `wrap_no_grad` are plain helpers so the logic is unit-testable without a GPU.

+Running DeepSeek-V4-Pro at scale
+--------------------------------
+
+DeepSeek-V4-Pro (61 layers, 384 routed experts, ~1.6 T parameters) runs through
+the same integration as Flash; what changes is scale. The reference launcher is
+``examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_pro_megatron.sh`` with two hardware
+profiles, ``HW=h100`` (64 nodes x 8 H100 80 GB) and ``HW=gb200`` (64 nodes x
+4 GB200). Both were validated with GRPO on DAPO-Math-17k; the numbers below are
+single-variable follow-ups on top of the respective profile.
+
+**Topology.** DSV4 fixes ``tensor_model_parallel_size=1`` on the Megatron side,
+so a Pro actor is sharded with pipeline and expert parallelism only: PP32 x EP8
+(DP2) on 512 H100s, PP16 x EP16 (DP1) on 256 GB200s. Stage 0 of the pipeline
+must hold the embedding and the three hash-routed layers; Megatron-Bridge
+generates the layout for PP16, the PP32 layout is spelled out in the launcher.
+A vLLM replica of Pro does not fit in one node, so the rollout uses cross-node
+data-parallel replicas (TP8 x DP8 x EP64 on H100, TP1 x DP32 x EP32 on GB200)
+under verl's ``expert_parallel_size = TP x DP`` rule. This needs verl ``main`` at or
+after #8234 (merged 2026-10-26): before it, vLLM 0.29 rejected the headless engines
+verl starts on the other nodes of a replica.
+
+**Memory.** With ``param_offload`` and ``optimizer_offload`` the GPU is rarely
+the constraint: the actor peaks at ~26 GB per H100 (response 4096, EP8; 77 GB
+per GPU including the sleeping vLLM worker on the stage-0 nodes) and 34-63 GB
+per GB200. The exception is response length 8192 on 80 GB GPUs, where
+stage 0 (embedding plus the three hash layers, ~11.6 B parameters at EP8) does
+not fit next to the ~17 GiB vLLM keeps resident after sleep; ``ACTOR_EP=16``
+(DP1) halves it. The host is the usual limit, because Megatron's
+HybridDeviceOptimizer keeps fp32 masters and Adam moments for every rank on the
+CPU (~12 bytes per parameter per rank, independent of DP). Three levers were
+needed:
+
+* ``override_ddp_config.grad_reduce_in_fp32=False`` (bf16 grad buffers); on
+  80 GB GPUs stage 0 does not fit without it.
+* ``use_precision_aware_optimizer=True`` with ``main_grads_dtype=bf16``: fp32
+  master shards move from the GPU into the offloaded optimizer state. Required
+  on H100, optional on GB200 (-30 % GPU and -22 % host memory at 4 layers,
+  ~+8 % step time). DSV4 then produces mixed bf16/fp32 gradient groups, which
+  Megatron-LM's grad-norm kernels do not accept until
+  https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7279 lands, and the quantized
+  main-param branch builds non-leaf shards until
+  https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8245 lands. The Megatron engine
+  applies runtime equivalents of both (``verl/models/mcore/patch.py``;
+  ``VERL_MEGATRON_OPTIMIZER_COMPAT=0`` disables them).
+* ``optimizer_offload_fraction < 1`` keeps part of the Adam state on the GPU
+  (fixed by https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8286).
+
+Keep the Ray object store small (32 GiB) when starting the cluster; its default
+of 30 % of host memory competes with the optimizer.
+
+**Checkpoints.** ``save_contents=[model,extra]`` is the default of the launcher:
+the optimizer state of Pro is ~22 TB, and resuming an offloaded optimizer needs
+verl ``main`` at or after #8235 (merged 2026-10-26). A model-only save is an HF
+export through Megatron-Bridge (~800 GB, ~30 min on 64 H100 nodes) or, when the
+actor was loaded with ``use_dist_checkpointing``, a bf16 Megatron
+dist-checkpoint (2.9 TB, ~40 s). On GB200 the save needs the precision-aware
+optimizer or 128 nodes (PP16 x EP32); otherwise the head node runs out of host
+memory during the save.
+
+**Rollout kernels.** verl defaults low-precision rollouts to DeepGEMM
+(``moe_backend=deep_gemm``); the Pro launcher overrides the MoE kernel to Marlin
+(W4A16) on both profiles. vLLM 0.29's DeepGEMM MXFP4 kernel is SM100+ only, so on
+H100 every vLLM worker fails at ``load_model`` with the default, and on GB200 the
+same kernel died with an illegal memory access in vLLM's profiling run at 10,240
+batched tokens (prompt 2048 + response 8192); where it ran (3,072 batched tokens)
+it was 5-9 % slower per step than Marlin for 64 samples. The other MXFP4 kernels
+are not options for a native DSV4 checkpoint: FlashInfer TRT-LLM cannot be
+refitted, and the FlashInfer CUTLASS kernel is not selectable (the CLI accepts
+only its BF16-activation variant, which rejects the MXFP4 weight scheme). The
+dense FP8 layers keep verl's DeepGEMM default (``linear_backend=deep_gemm``).
+
+**What the reward means.** On DAPO-Math-17k the per-step
+``critic/score/mean`` of Pro is almost exactly ``1 - 2 x clip_ratio``: in 192
+inspected samples every response that reached a final answer was correct and
+every truncated one was scored -1. The score therefore tracks the truncation
+rate, not accuracy; track the accuracy of completed responses separately
+(``trainer.rollout_data_dir``) and expect to need harder prompts or a larger
+response budget before the curve moves.
+
+**Long runs.** On clusters with a wall-clock limit, run the job as a chain of
+segments with ``trainer.save_freq`` and ``trainer.resume_mode=auto``; each
+segment resumes from the newest ``global_step_*`` and the first step after a
+resume costs 1.5-4x a steady step (initial weight sync plus every JIT the new
+job has to redo; ~2x on GB200, ~3.7x on H100).
+
+Measured on the two profiles (verl ``main`` a4b9354 + #8234, Megatron-Bridge 0.6.2, vLLM 0.29.0, Marlin MoE kernels, R3, 3 GRPO steps each):
+
+.. list-table::
+   :header-rows: 1
+
+   * - Profile
+     - Response length
+     - Steady step time
+     - of which ``gen`` / ``update_weights``
+     - rollout/actor log-prob Pearson (R3)
+     - Host peak per node
+   * - ``h100`` (64 x 8 H100, PP32 x EP8, rollout TP8 x DP8)

+     - ~690 s (first step 2585 s with JIT)
+     - ~280 s / ~235 s

+     - 558 GB on the two pipeline-stage-0 nodes, 244-409 GB on the others (mean 383 GB)
+   * - ``gb200`` (64 x 4 GB200, PP16 x EP16, rollout DP32)
+     - 8192
+     - ~965 s (first step 1991 s)
+     - ~500 s / ~251 s
+     - 0.998
+     - 929 GB on the head node (stock optimizer; no headroom for a save at this shape, see Checkpoints)

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Megatron-Core optimizer compatibility for quantized checkpoints with the
+# precision-aware optimizer (DeepSeek-V4 and similar FP8 / MXFP4 models).
+#
+# Two upstream fixes are pending; until they land, verl applies runtime
+# equivalents once per process (set VERL_MEGATRON_OPTIMIZER_COMPAT=0 to skip):
+#
+# 1. https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8245 -- for quantized model
+#    params without ``get_high_precision_init_val``, ``DistributedOptimizer``
+#    builds the fp32 main-param shard as ``model_param.float().view(-1)[a:b]``
+#    under autograd, i.e. a non-leaf view with ``requires_grad=True``.  The
+#    default optimizer path never validates it, but ``optimizer_cpu_offload=True``
+#    rebuilds the HybridDeviceOptimizer through ``torch.optim.Optimizer.__init__``,
+#    whose ``add_param_group`` raises ``can't optimize a non-leaf Tensor``.
+#    Building the groups under ``torch.no_grad()`` yields grad_fn-free shards;
+#    the recorded grad_fn was never used (Megatron copies grads into the main
+#    params by hand).
+# 2. https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7279 -- ``get_grad_norm_fp32`` /
+#    ``clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32`` hand one list of gradients to a single
+#    multi-tensor kernel that is dispatched on the dtype of the first tensor.
+#    With ``use_precision_aware_optimizer`` + bf16 main grads, bf16 params expose
+#    bf16 decoupled grads while the model's native fp32 params (DSV4's hc
+#    alpha/bias, ape, attn_sink) keep fp32 grads: the kernel reads past the
+#    smaller elements and dies with an illegal memory access.  The replacement
+#    runs the kernel once per dtype group and combines the partial norms; a
+#    single-dtype list is forwarded to the original function unchanged.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def wrap_no_grad(cls, name: str, marker: str) -> bool:
+    """Wrap ``cls.<name>`` so it runs under ``torch.no_grad()``.
+
+    Handles plain functions, classmethods and staticmethods.  Returns False when
+    the attribute is missing or already wrapped (``marker`` set on ``cls``).
+    """
+    import logging
+
+    import torch
+
+    if getattr(cls, marker, False):
+        return False
+    if name not in cls.__dict__:
+        # Inherited (or renamed) upstream: nothing to wrap here.  Say so, because a silent skip would
+        # look like a successful patch to anyone reading the logs.
+        logging.getLogger(__name__).warning(
+            "%s.%s is not defined on the class itself (inherited or renamed); no-grad wrap skipped", cls.__name__, name
+        )
+        return False
+    raw = cls.__dict__[name]
+    kind = type(raw) if isinstance(raw, (classmethod, staticmethod)) else None
+    func = raw.__func__ if kind is not None else raw
+
+    def wrapped(*args, **kwargs):
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            return func(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    wrapped.__name__ = getattr(func, "__name__", name)
+    wrapped.__doc__ = getattr(func, "__doc__", None)
+    setattr(cls, name, kind(wrapped) if kind is not None else wrapped)
+    setattr(cls, marker, True)
+    return True
+
+
+def apply_distributed_optimizer_no_grad_main_params_patch() -> bool:
+    """Build ``DistributedOptimizer`` main-param groups under ``no_grad`` (Megatron-LM #8245)."""
+    import logging
+
+    try:
+        from megatron.core.optimizer.distrib_optimizer import DistributedOptimizer
+    except ImportError:
+        return False
+    applied = wrap_no_grad(
+        DistributedOptimizer, "_build_model_and_main_param_groups", "_verl_no_grad_main_params_patch"
+    )
+    if applied:
+        # WARNING on purpose: Ray workers do not surface INFO, and users need to see that the patch is live.
+        logging.getLogger(__name__).warning(
+            "Patched DistributedOptimizer._build_model_and_main_param_groups to run under no_grad "
+            "(Megatron-LM #8245: non-leaf fp32 main-param shards for quantized params)"
+        )
+    return applied
+
+
+def make_dtype_safe_grad_fns(cg):
+    """Return per-dtype-group versions of ``get_grad_norm_fp32`` / ``clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32``.
+
+    ``cg`` is ``megatron.core.optimizer.clip_grads`` (or any object exposing the same
+    names); it is a parameter so the logic can be unit-tested without a GPU.
+    """
+    import logging
+
+    import torch
+
+    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+    orig_norm = cg.get_grad_norm_fp32
+    orig_clip = cg.clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32
+    announced = {"norm": False, "clip": False}
+
+    def _group_by_dtype(tensors):
+        groups = {}
+        for t in tensors:
+            groups.setdefault(t.dtype, []).append(t)
+        return groups
+
+    def get_grad_norm_fp32(grads_for_norm, norm_type=2, grad_stats_parallel_group=None):
+        if isinstance(grads_for_norm, torch.Tensor):
+            grads_for_norm = [grads_for_norm]
+        groups = _group_by_dtype(grads_for_norm)
+        if len(groups) <= 1 or float(norm_type) != 2.0:
+            return orig_norm(grads_for_norm, norm_type, grad_stats_parallel_group)
+        if not announced["norm"]:
+            logger.warning("dtype-safe grad norm active: groups=%s", {str(k): len(v) for k, v in groups.items()})
+            announced["norm"] = True
+        data_parallel_group = None
+        for g in grads_for_norm:
+            data_parallel_group = cg.get_data_parallel_group_if_dtensor(g, data_parallel_group)
+        total = None
+        for gs in groups.values():
+            gs = [cg.to_local_if_dtensor(g) for g in gs]
+            dummy_overflow_buf = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int, device=gs[0].device)
+            grad_norm, _ = cg.multi_tensor_applier(cg.l2_norm_impl, dummy_overflow_buf, [gs], False)
+            sq = grad_norm.float() ** 2.0
+            total = sq if total is None else total + sq
+        if data_parallel_group:
+            torch.distributed.all_reduce(total, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.SUM, group=data_parallel_group)
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(total, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.SUM, group=grad_stats_parallel_group)
+        if cg.multi_tensor_scale_tensor_impl is not None:
+            return total.pow(0.5)
+        return total.item() ** 0.5
+
+    def clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32(parameters, max_norm, total_norm, use_decoupled_grad=False):
+        grads = []
+        for param in parameters:
+            if use_decoupled_grad:
+                if getattr(param, "decoupled_grad", None) is not None:
+                    assert param.decoupled_grad.dtype in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16)
+                    grads.append(cg.to_local_if_dtensor(param.decoupled_grad).detach())
+            elif param.grad is not None:
+                grads.append(cg.to_local_if_dtensor(param.grad).detach())
+        groups = _group_by_dtype(grads)
+        if len(groups) <= 1:
+            return orig_clip(parameters, max_norm, total_norm, use_decoupled_grad)
+        if not announced["clip"]:

@linmuchuiyang It's unexpected that vLLM can't enable DeepGEMM for DeepSeek-V4 both in Hopper/Blackwell, let me have a check.

@aoshen02 @ISEEKYAN done train-rollout kernel bitwise alignment on DeepSeek-V4 in https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-14-train-inference-consistency, I think they used deep_gemm kernel for both linear and moe.

@wuxibin89 Thanks for looking. I believe the difference is the checkpoint, not the kernel:

- The recipe in that blog trains **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base**, whose routed experts are FP8 (`"expert_dtype": "fp8"` in its `config.json`; the post says "the routed experts' FP8 grouped GEMM"). For that checkpoint vLLM runs DeepGEMM's FP8 grouped GEMM for the MoE, which exists on SM90 and SM100, so `linear_backend=deep_gemm` + `moe_backend=deep_gemm` is the right default on both — and the change proposed in #8381 keeps it for every `expert_dtype: fp8` model.
- The post-trained **DeepSeek-V4-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Pro** ship MXFP4 experts (`"expert_dtype": "fp4"`). For them vLLM maps `moe_backend=deep_gemm` to `DeepGemmFP4Experts` (`m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous`), whose `_supports_current_device` requires SM100 or SM120 (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/deep_gemm_moe.py`, unchanged in v0.32.0). That is the H100 `load_model` error in #8381; the FP8 dense layers still use DeepGEMM there (`--linear_backend deep_gemm` stays).
- On GB200 the FP4 DeepGEMM path does run for Pro: fine at 4,096 batched tokens (8297634), `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in `profile_run` at 10,240 (8183203), and ~24 % slower generation than Marlin where it runs. That part may well be a vLLM/DeepGEMM bug as you suspect; we will re-run it on vLLM 0.32.0 (#8390) and report in #8381.

So the example keeps `moe_backend=marlin` for the MXFP4 experts of the released Pro checkpoint, and `linear_backend` at verl's DeepGEMM default.
